💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that another Thanksgiving week is upon us, which means tens of millions of Americans will once again travel by plane, train, and automobile to see their loved ones.
  • Sources indicate that another Thanksgiving week is upon us, which means tens of millions of Americans will once again travel by plane, train, and automobile to see their loved ones.
  • “After three years of record highs, the number of travelers is slightly lower partly because of higher travel costs this year,” says Stacey Barber, vice president of AAA travel.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that another Thanksgiving week is upon us, which means tens of millions of Americans will once again travel by plane, train, and automobile to see their loved ones. However, this Thanksgiving period will be a little different than in recent years—at least when it comes to transportation. That’s because the American Automobile Association (AAA) says that, for the first time in several years, fewer Americans will be traveling. “After three years of record highs, the number of travelers is slightly lower partly because of higher travel costs this year,” says Stacey Barber, vice president of AAA travel. “But travelers won’t notice much of a difference on the roads and at the airports, since projected volumes remain near record levels.”  That means that despite fewer travelers, the roads are still expected to be packed at times. With that in mind, here are the best and worst times to travel by car over the 2026 Thanksgiving period. Best times to hit the roads for the Thanksgiving travel period For the 2026 Thanksgiving period, AAA expects 72.9 million people to travel to their holiday destinations by car. That’s down from last year’s 73.1 million automobile travelers, but still a significant amount. AAA defines the 2026 Thanksgiving period as the seven days lasting from Tuesday, November 24 to Monday, November 30, 2026. But despite the expected 72.9 million road travelers, how congested the streets will be depends heavily on when you travel during the period. AAA says these are the best times to be on the road (ie: the times with the expected lowest congestion) over the period, according to transportation data and insights provider INRIX data compiled by the auto organization: Tuesday, November 24: Before 1:00 PM Wednesday, November 25: Before 12:00 PM  Thursday, November 26 (Thanksgiving): Minimal Traffic Impact Expected  Friday, November 27: Before 12:00 PM  Saturday, November 28: Before 11:00 AM  Sunday, November 29: Before 11:00 AM  Monday, November 30: Before 1:00 PM  Worst times to hit the roads for the Thanksgiving travel period INRIX data shows that the worst days to travel over the Thanksgiving period—that is, the days the congestion is expected to be the highest—are the Tuesday and Wednesday before Thanksgiving, and the Sunday and Monday after. Those are the days when most people choose to travel to and from their holiday destinations. As for the individual times that are expected to be the worst to travel by car, those are: Tuesday, November 24: 2:00 PM to 8:00 PM  Wednesday, November 25: 12:00 PM to 7:00 PM  Thursday, November 26 (Thanksgiving): Minimal Traffic Impact Expected  Friday, November 27: 1:00 PM to 7:00 PM  Saturday, November 28: 12:00 PM to 9:00 PM  Sunday, November 29: 12:00 PM to 8:00 PM  Monday, November 30: 2:00 PM to 7:00 PM  Fewer total travelers are expected over the Thanksgiving 2026 period When combining all modes of transportation—auto, air, and “other,” which includes bus, boat, and train—AAA says 81.48 million people in America are expected to travel over the 2026 Thanksgiving period. That’s about 121,000 fewer than the 81.61 million who traveled during the 2025 Thanksgiving period. Still, 2026’s expected numbers far surpass the 77.78 million people who traveled in 2019, the last year before the pandemic. The expected decline in travelers this year is mainly due to higher travel costs, especially gas prices, AAA says. Besides a decline of about 200,000 car travelers, AAA says there will also be a drop in air travelers by about 0.2% to 5.96 million (versus 5.97 million in 2025). However, more people will travel by “other” modes during this period than last year. “Other” includes travel by bus, train, and cruise. In the 2026 Thanksgiving period, the other travel segment is expected to reach 2.6 million travelers—up 4.1% from 2.49 million in 2025.

Latest Update: 6 tips to use this Thanksgiving when family asks about your career

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, evan Reece has a few strategies for handling unwelcome questions about his career when he gathers with family. He founded and ran a ski lift ticket platform for 15 years, but it went out of business during the COVID-19 pandemic. Reece then started a career management platform. He’s its sole employee and earns less than he did before.At family parties, he sometimes feels pressure to explain why he doesn’t get a full-time job working for someone else. When he’s asked such questions, he reminds himself that people usually ask because they care.“Oftentimes, if we’re stressed about something that we don’t have an answer to, the question feels like an interrogation, when that’s rarely the intention of the person asking the question,” mentioned Reece, 48, who runs the career management platform Truest.me.A simple “How’s your job going?” can feel like an ambush when you’re unemployed, underemployed or working in jobs your friends and relatives don’t understand or may regard as frivolous. These queries can bring up painful experiences like layoffs. Advice can sound like criticism to recent graduates in a seemingly impenetrable job market, while curiosity about someone’s income can feel like judgment.Even inquiries motivated by a genuine desire to connect can come across as invasive or awkward in a group setting.With holiday gatherings approaching, here are some tips and potential scripts to help you handle tricky career conversations with relatives and feel less defensive. The same strategies can be applied when faced with scrutiny about getting married or having children. Anticipate questions and strategy responses in advance Have a short, confident response or two ready for the job-related queries you think might come up, said Melody Wilding, an executive coach and author of “Managing Up.”For example, if you’re unemployed, you could say, “I’m taking time to find the right fit and not rushing into something new.” Or if you’ve made an unconventional career move, say, “I know it’s not what everyone would choose, but I’m excited about it,” Wilding said.“Then redirect the conversation nicely. You might say, ‘Tell me about you,’ or ‘I’d love to hear about your recent trip,'” she added. Be a boomerang when fielding questions Turning the inquiries around on the questioner can deflect attention and be entertaining.“If someone is willing to ask you a question that requires tremendous vulnerability out of you, then they should be willing to answer one too,” Reece said.When a relative asks if you’re “still job searching” or “Why did you leave a good job?” get curious before you get defensive, Wilding suggested. Instead of immediately responding to their question, try to understand the motivation behind it by countering, “Why do you ask?” or “What makes you say that?” Wilding said.“Maybe they’re just making conversation, which saves you from launching into a full defense of your choices,” she said. Turn it into a game If someone asks about an unstable job or recent layoff, you can say it’s been challenging and then suggest, “Let’s play a game. Everybody tell a story about the worst job they ever had,” Reece said. “Anybody who’s ever worked has a story. And they’re usually amazing.”For recent graduates or those who are trying to figure out what’s next, you could be honest about your uncertainty and reply, “Everybody go around and talk about a time in their career when they weren’t sure what to do next and what you did,” Reece suggested. Let others take the spotlight Hope Bond, 53, spent a decade working as an editor in the magazine industry. She left the field for a few years to raise her young children, then did some freelance editing jobs. When she sought to return to full-time work in 2020, she couldn’t find a position. Bond began working as a site manager for a movie production location in 2024.She loves the job, despite its erratic hours, instability and hourly pay. But at gatherings with her family of lawyers and bankers, she often felt singled out by probing questions about her work.After years of answering their questions, she now redirects them and encourages others to be the star of the conversation, especially her children.“I stay on the periphery. The younger generations are the ones who are bringing the great energy, so I like them to have the floor,” Bond said. “I don’t insert myself into conversation if we’re talking about career or money. Those are my two boundaries. Okay, so here’s the deal (literally): last year’s Moto G Stylus (2025) is on sale right now on Amazon for just $199, and if you desperately need a digital writing tool with your phone, it’s a good buy.

That is the short answer; the long answer is a little more complicated, as due to some concerns with the 2026 model, you are missing out on exactly…nothing. Yes, at under $200, you are getting essentially the same phone because Motorola decided that, due to RAM and storage shortages and price hikes, the newer model would forgo any major upgrades. The 2026 model starts at $499, so if you had your eye on it, yeah, it’s a silly way to waste $300 in our opinion.

According to recent reports, it has the same Snapdragon 6 Gen 3 processor, 8GB RAM, and 128GB storage. There’s a 120Hz display too and the good news is you get a microSD card slot to expand the storage if you desperately need it. Other notable features include a 5,000mAh battery, 68W wired charging, 15W wireless charging, a 50MP camera setup, and, as of writing, it should be due for an Android 16 upgrade.

Industry observers note that the star of the show of the Moto G Stylus (2025) is the stylus. It boils down to this: if you want a phone that isn’t a Galaxy Ultra, then this is the only other line that makes sense for document signers.

However, there are better deals out there. I think the Galaxy A56, at just $299, is an incredible offer right now and way more deserving of your hard-earned cash. Even so, if you want clean software or that stylus, the Moto G Stylus (2025) at $199 is at least an option especially for a family member or a backup to your existing phone.

So I bought the smallest Hostinger VPS strategy, deployed a Node.js app in Docker, and handed the DevOps work to Hostinger Agent, the AI assistant built into the dashboard.

Below is what that felt like step by step and whether it’s worth locking in a price before they climb further.

Apps built with AI coding tools. Claude Code and Cursor get you to a working Node.js or Python app fast, then leave you wondering where to put it. Think n8n workflows, a scheduled scraper, or your own agent in a Docker container. Hostinger even has an “Ubuntu 24.04 with Claude Code” template: SSH in, run claude /login, and the agent keeps working after you close your laptop.

Sources indicate that APIs, backends and databases for side projects. A Postgres instance, a Redis cache and a small API behind a reverse proxy fit comfortably on a mid-sized plan. You pick the versions, the extensions and the backup schedule.

In a recent development, client sites and stores. Freelancers outgrow shared hosting when one client needs a custom PHP extension or a WooCommerce store starts to crawl. A VPS with cPanel or Plesk, or a WordPress or WooCommerce template, keeps client work isolated and under your control.

If you’d rather not build anything from scratch, the Docker Manager catalog listed 1,017 one-click templates when I checked, including 93 under AI/ML and 162 under Developer tools.

For this Hostinger VPS review, the question I cared about was simple: how long from “Choose plan” to an app on the internet? On KVM 1, the entry plan, it was about 12 minutes. Here’s each step with rough timings.

I went with KVM 1: 1 vCPU, 4 GB RAM, 50 GB NVMe storage and 4 TB of bandwidth. On the Black Friday deal it costs $6.49/mo, paid upfront as $155.76 for 24 months, and renews at $11.99/mo.

The five-minute estimate was about right. The “you’re ready” screen then gives you two ways in: the VPS dashboard, or a pre-filled ssh root@ command. It also offers a free domain for a year to use as the server’s hostname.

The overview demonstrates the OS, strategy, CPU, RAM, disk and bandwidth at a glance, with Docker Manager, Backups & Monitoring, Security and DNS Manager in the side menu.

In a recent development, every server also gets a hostname under hstgr.cloud (mine was srvXXXXXXX.hstgr.cloud), which came in handy later for SSL. I’ve masked my hostname as srvXXXXXXX throughout and blurred IP addresses in the screenshots.

In a recent development, plain Ubuntu doesn’t ship with Docker. Open Docker Manager in hPanel and it installs Docker for you with one click. From there you can deploy apps from a Compose file, a repository URL or the one-click catalog.

Sources indicate that click Web console and you’re logged in as root in a browser tab, with Hostinger Agent in a panel beside it. You don’t need an SSH client or keys. The login banner flagged 33 pending updates, 23 of them security fixes; more on that later. A quick docker --version confirmed Docker 29.9.3 was ready.

Here’s the whole app: a tiny HTTP server with a health check, and a Dockerfile on Node.js 24, a supported LTS line.

Then build it, run it and check it:.

Recent findings suggest that the build took 8.3 seconds, including pulling node:24-alpine, and the health check answered straight away. The --restart unless-stopped flag brings the container back after a crash or reboot, which I tested later.

In a recent development, that’s a working app, but on plain HTTP, on a high port, with no TLS. Getting it production-ready is the DevOps part I handed to the AI.

In a recent development, an AI-managed VPS isn’t the same as a traditional managed VPS. You still get a self-managed server with full root access, but Hostinger Agent does the work you’d normally do yourself. Agent (previously called Kodee) is an MCP-powered assistant that lives in the dashboard and beside the AI web terminal, and it’s included at no extra cost. You can also connect Claude or Cursor to your server through Hostinger’s MCP server.

I gave it three tasks in plain English.

My prompt: “Check that Docker is installed, then set up a reverse proxy with a free SSL certificate so my demo-app container (port 3000) is served at https://srvXXXXXXX.hstgr.cloud.”.

It has been revealed that it started by looking around: the Docker and Compose versions, which ports were in use, whether a web server was already running, and the OS release. Then it installed Caddy from Caddy’s official repository, configured the proxy and made sure ufw allowed web traffic.

It read Caddy’s logs to confirm the Let’s Encrypt certificate, which arrived in about 6 seconds. Finally it tested its own work: HTTPS returned 200, and plain HTTP returned a 308 redirect. The whole task took about two minutes.

To give it a real fault, I ran docker stop demo-app and reloaded the site. Then I asked why it was returning a 502 and to fix it.

Industry observers note that in a single command, it checked the container state (Exited (137)) and searched Caddy’s logs, where it found connect: connection refused on port 3000. It restarted the container, confirmed /health and HTTPS were back, and even pointed to my docker stop in the terminal history. It also explained that --restart unless-stopped covers crashes and reboots, but not a manual stop.

In a recent development, A tip it didn’t mention: exit code 137 means Docker had to force-kill the container, because Node running as PID 1 ignores SIGTERM. Add --init to docker run for clean, instant shutdowns.

This was the most impressive answer. ufw already allowed only those three ports, but Agent noticed port 3000 was still reachable from the internet, because Docker-published ports bypass ufw rules.

Sources indicate that it recreated the container bound to 127.0.0.1:3000, so the app is only reachable through Caddy, and confirmed with an external port check. It left DNS, time sync and Caddy’s local admin port running, explaining that stopping them would break DNS and time sync.

Sources indicate that then I asked it to reboot the server. First it checked that Docker and Caddy start on boot and that the container’s restart policy was set, then it rebooted. The site came back over HTTPS without any help from me.

Nothing I asked for was destructive, so Agent just got on with it: the firewall change, the container rebuild and the reboot all ran without a confirmation prompt.

Recent findings suggest that the Agent panel says so upfront, noting that terminal commands can run without one. For destructive actions such as reinstalling the OS or restoring a backup, Hostinger’s FAQ says Agent always asks for confirmation first.

One thing worth knowing: to close port 3000, Agent removed and recreated my container. That was harmless for a stateless demo, but a container that keeps data without a volume would lose it. Take a snapshot before major jobs, and keep the panel in view.

So 4 GB is plenty for one or two small apps. Move to 8 GB on KVM 2 once you add Coolify, a database, or n8n with its own Postgres, because those are the services that eat memory.

Finding a cheap VPS got harder in 2026, because memory got expensive. AI data centres are buying up DRAM, and hosts are passing the cost on. In April 2026, Hetzner raised cloud server prices by up to 37%, citing hardware costs, then raised prices again in June. On the same April date, OVHcloud’s entry VPS went from $4.90 to $7.60, a 55% jump. Nobody can promise where VPS prices go next, but the trend this year has been up.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, jensen Huang has been under a spotlight for weeks, but after the 11-day period of disorder that included the resignation and reinstatement of the Nvidia executive, the company’s board is joining him at the center of scrutiny.The 10-person board voted unanimously to rehire Huang as Nvidia’s president, CEO and a fellow board member, writing in an announcement Monday that the decision emerged after discussions with Huang and “input from senior levels of the United States government.” President Donald Trump mentioned he believes his intervention was crucial to the reinstatement.Just six days earlier, the board was singing a different tune. Board members had unanimously accepted Huang’s resignation following his admission that he had an affair with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy. The board did not intend to reinstate him, Nvidia Chairman Harvey Jones said at the start of a quarterly earnings call.“To bow to pressure to bring someone back who has hurt the reputation of the company is crazy,” said Kathleen Day, a lecturer at Johns Hopkins Carey Business School.The board’s stunning reversal has spurred questions about its independence and what Trump’s role means for the meeting of business and politics. Concerns swirl about corporate governance and Trump’s intervention Nvidia’s board includes both business leaders with longstanding ties to the company and a group of more recent additions who have experience at big-name companies including Taco Bell, PepsiCo and Eli Lilly.Some experts have called for the board to resign in the wake of the havoc.Day, who has expertise in financial crises and corporate governance, emphasized that the board has a duty to represent shareholders, not the CEO.“The shareholders should demand a new board,” she said.Corporate governance experts say long tenures for board members can compromise their independence. Under the rules of the New York Stock Exchange and the Nasdaq, companies are required to have a majority of directors who are independent.“Traditionally, it’s a good practice” to limit how long people can sit on a board, said Nada Kakabadse, professor of policy, governance and ethics at the University of Reading’s Henley Business School. “They should be eight years maximum. Four years, plus another four years if they’re performing well. But beyond that, they really become not independent anymore, right?”It’s not unusual for U.S. tech bosses to stuff their boards with allies or high-profile figures who might not be aware of what’s happening at the company, Kakabadse said.American business has a culture of “leader heroes” — entrepreneurs who founded companies and are seen as the only ones who can steer them through tough times, she said. But at some point, the companies can get so big that “you need proper corporate structure, you need proper governance.”Many people are also questioning what “input” the company received from senior government leaders and why it persuaded the board to make a complete turnaround.“The board should have listened to the president’s request and stuck to its position that it was time to find a new CEO,” said Peter Cohan, an associate professor of management practice at Babson College. “In my opinion, by giving in to Trump, the board is endangering the company. That’s because Huang has seen that he can do anything he wants, and he will get away with it.”The idea of an independent board of experts looking out for the long-term interests of the company and its shareholders “sort of goes out the window” if the sitting president “essentially tells them what to do,” said Daniel Kinderman, a professor of political science and international relations at the University of Delaware.“This is really the mark of crony capitalism, right?” he said.Kinderman said the episode might “open the door a little bit more for more aggressive actions on behalf of elected representatives” in their relationships with businesses. Lawmakers call for accountability from the board The Nvidia saga has made waves in Washington, particularly in conversations around export controls. Huang’s affair raised questions about Nvidia’s compliance with those restrictions. The reinstatement has renewed fervor on Capitol Hill for more transparency from both Huang and the board.Elected officials from both parties were quick to respond to the reinstatement with criticism and skepticism.Democratic Sen. Elizabeth Warren, the incoming chair of the Senate Banking Committee, said the decision to bring Huang back was “reckless.” She wrote in a statement Monday that it does not change the fact that Huang, Nvidia executives and the company’s board “still owe Congress answers.”Sen. Kirsten Gillibrand, a New York Democrat, called for both Huang and the board to testify publicly to Congress. “A boardroom vote does not resolve a national security risk,” she said in a statement Monday.California Attorney General Rob Bonta, who is investigating Nvidia in connection with Huang’s affair, said Tuesday in an interview with CNBC that the president’s intervention “does not bode well for enforcement of the law by the federal government without fear, without favor.”The California Department of Justice said Thursday that it is asking Nvidia whether its advanced chips or confidential information may have gone to China and whether Nvidia misled investors and the public. Some members joined the Nvidia board in the 1990s Two board members, Mark Stevens and Tench Coxe, joined the board in 1993 when Nvidia was founded. Stevens and Coxe were both previously venture capitalists who made early investments in Nvidia.Two other long-serving board members, Jones and Brooke Seawell, are the former chief executive and chief financial officer, respectively, of Synopsys, which makes chip-design software and counted Nvidia as its first customer. Jones joined Nvidia’s board in 1993, while Seawell joined four years later.Stephen Neal, who’s designated as the board’s “lead independent director,” joined in 2019. He’s the chairman emeritus of Cooley LLP, Nvidia’s longtime law firm, and has advised the company in “various governance matters,” according to his bio.Other board members have less of a direct link to Nvidia.Melissa Lora, former president of Taco Bell International, spent 31 years at the fast food company and joined Nvidia’s board in 2023. Aarti Shah, formerly a senior vice president and chief digital officer at pharmaceutical company Eli Lilly, joined in 2020.John Dabiri, an engineering professor at the California Institute of Technology whose lab researches fluid mechanics, was added to the board in 2020. Dawn Hudson was the NFL’s chief marketing officer and a former CEO of Pepsi-Cola’s North American division who’s been on the board since 2013. Suzanne Nora Johnson was a vice chairman at Goldman Sachs who joined the board in July.None of the board members provided comment in response to requests from The Associated Press. Jensen Huang has been under a spotlight for weeks, but after the 11-day period of disorder that included the resignation and reinstatement of the Nvidia executive, the company’s board is joining him at the center of scrutiny.The 10-person board voted unanimously to rehire Huang as Nvidia’s president, CEO and a fellow board member, writing in an announcement Monday that the decision emerged after discussions with Huang and “input from senior levels of the United States government.” President Donald Trump noted he believes his intervention was crucial to the reinstatement.Just six days earlier, the board was singing a different tune. Board members had unanimously accepted Huang’s resignation following his admission that he had an affair with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy. The board did not intend to reinstate him, Nvidia Chairman Harvey Jones said at the start of a quarterly earnings call.“To bow to pressure to bring someone back who has hurt the reputation of the company is crazy,” said Kathleen Day, a lecturer at Johns Hopkins Carey Business School.The board’s stunning reversal has spurred questions about its independence and what Trump’s role means for the meeting of business and politics.

Nvidia’s board includes both business leaders with longstanding ties to the company and a group of more recent additions who have experience at massive-name companies including Taco Bell, PepsiCo and Eli Lilly.Some experts have called for the board to resign in the wake of the havoc.Day, who has expertise in financial crises and corporate governance, emphasized that the board has a duty to represent shareholders, not the CEO.“The shareholders should demand a latest board,” she mentioned.Corporate governance experts say long tenures for board members can compromise their independence. Under the rules of the New York Stock Exchange and the Nasdaq, companies are required to have a majority of directors who are independent.“Traditionally, it’s a good practice” to limit how long people can sit on a board, said Nada Kakabadse, professor of policy, governance and ethics at the University of Reading’s Henley Business School. “They should be eight years maximum. Four years, plus another four years if they’re performing well. But beyond that, they really become not independent anymore, right?”It’s not unusual for U.S. tech bosses to stuff their boards with allies or high-profile figures who might not be aware of what’s happening at the company, Kakabadse said.American business has a culture of “leader heroes” — entrepreneurs who founded companies and are seen as the only ones who can steer them through tough times, she said. But at some point, the companies can get so big that “you need proper corporate structure, you need proper governance.”Many people are also questioning what “input” the company received from senior government leaders and why it persuaded the board to make a complete turnaround.“The board should have listened to the president’s request and stuck to its position that it was time to find a new CEO,” said Peter Cohan, an associate professor of management practice at Babson College. “In my opinion, by giving in to Trump, the board is endangering the company. That’s because Huang has seen that he can do anything he wants, and he will get away with it.”The idea of an independent board of experts looking out for the long-term interests of the company and its shareholders “sort of goes out the window” if the sitting president “essentially tells them what to do,” said Daniel Kinderman, a professor of political science and international relations at the University of Delaware.“This is really the mark of crony capitalism, right?” he said.Kinderman said the episode might “open the door a little bit more for more aggressive actions on behalf of elected representatives” in their relationships with businesses.

The Nvidia saga has made waves in Washington, particularly in conversations around export controls. Huang’s affair raised questions about Nvidia’s compliance with those restrictions. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Australia’s Parliament on Wednesday passed online safety laws that could expose tech giants to multibillion-dollar fines for failing to prevent foreseeable online harms.The United States and the Australian opposition party warned that the legislation would lead to censorship of lawful speech.The Digital Duty of Care Act requires Significant Tech to proactively reduce the risk of harm before it occurs, according to an Australian government statement. Australian online law falls in line with EU and British legislation The legislation is similar to the European Union’s Digital Services Act, passed in 2022, and the United Kingdom’s Online Safety Act passed a year later.The legislation became law in the House of Representatives, where the center-left Labor Party government commands a majority, by 97 votes to 43.Prime Minister Anthony Albanese told Parliament the law would stand as a “powerful instrument to protect our children and our society from online harms by placing the onus on the tech platforms to ensure a safer online environment.”“This is a victory for our children and young people. The dangers were unforeseen when the digital world was young,” Albanese said. “But now that the digital world has matured, they can be easily recognized and they can be remedied.” Opposition leader vows to repeal ‘authoritarian’ law Opposition leader Angus Taylor told Parliament he would repeal the legislation if his conservative Liberal Party wins elections in 2028. Taylor described the legislation as “authoritarian.”“This bill is a blank check for political censorship,” Taylor told Parliament. “The bill is an attack on free speech that is absolutely central to our democracy.”The government struck a deal with the minor Greens party on Tuesday to get the legislation through the Senate, where no party holds a majority.“Today, the safety and wellbeing of Australians and their children have finally been put ahead of Big Tech’s bottom line,” Greens chief negotiator Sarah Hanson-Young said in a statement after the bill passed the Senate by 36 votes to 23.“My message to Big Tech companies is, it’s time to make your platforms safe or we will see you in court,” she added.The Australian legislation sets minimum safety standards for online services, including games, apps and artificial intelligence chatbots, requiring them to protect Australians from seriously harmful material and conduct, the government said.The Greens’ amendments include increasing maximum penalties for breaches from 109 million Australian dollars ($72 million), as the government originally proposed, to 5% of a tech company’s global revenue.U.S. Ambassador to Australia David Brat said on Tuesday the then-proposed laws would “impose disproportionate compliance burdens on American companies relative to competitors.”“Vaguely defined ‘harms,’ backed by penalties of up to 5% of global revenue, will push platforms to censor lawful speech,” Brat posted on social media. —Rod Mcguirk, Associated Press.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

McDonald’s to gamers: We are so hip. Ahead of the highly anticipated release of Grand Theft Auto VI last week, the fast food giant confirmed that U.S.-based gamers can now place an order on Discord to be delivered by Uber Eats. And to demonstrate just how hip the septuagenarian tech giant is, the announcement appealed directly to gamers with text speak—it’s littered with derivatives of “u” in lieu of “you.” “McDonald’s is showing up on Discord to make it a little easier to get ur McDelivery order when breaking from ur servers just isn’t an option,” the company noted in a press release. Yes, that’s verbatim from the Chicago-based company—the sort of appeal that could well remind some people of the “How do you do, fellow kids?” meme featuring actor Steve Buscemi from an episode of 30 Rock. Surprisingly, the announcement didn’t elicit many jeers from the Reddit crowd of Discord consumers, where many people drew comparisons to now-defunct collaborations between fast food chains and gaming consoles that similarly let gamers seamlessly order food. Hype around the end of a 13-year wait for a newly introduced edition of the popular game surely warranted being a little cringey. The company didn’t immediately respond to a request for comment from Fast Company regarding how popular the new ordering option has been thus far, but The New York Times reported that both DoorDash and Uber Eats experienced double-digit spikes in orders in the hours after the game was released. MCDONALD’S LATEST MOVES Even if it’s only a marketing ploy, the Discord ordering optionality illustrates just how much McDonald’s wants to show up for customers. Earlier this month, company executives revealed plans to introduce new value-oriented meal bundles next year to appeal to cash-strapped customers. And its nearly decade-long collaboration with Uber Eats is nothing to scoff at. Earlier this month, the two companies announced that their nearly decade-long partnership will expand delivery to 14 new markets, adding to its existing 30-country market. In a more buttoned-up press release intended for investors, Mason Smoot, senior vice president of global franchising and delivery, said its home delivery option—dubbed McDelivery—is a $20 billion-plus global business each year. Even though the company has been trying for more than a year to overcome a challenging market with its U.S. customers, it’s been making a wide range of attempts to lure them back—and that’s seemingly resonating with investors. While McDonald’s shares are still down for the year, they’ve surged more than 14% in the past month. During that same period, the broader S&P 500 Index has slumped nearly 8%.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Frontier AI models that have yet to be released by OpenAI and Anthropic are reportedly reaching the point where employees believe they cannot be safely released or controlled, employees reportedly say.

Axios cites “more than two dozen” employees inside of OpenAI and Anthropic who are sounding warnings around unreleased models from both companies.

While both OpenAI’s GPT and Anthropic’s Claude public models are increasingly powerful, these employees say that new models behind the scenes are starting to beat out the technical solutions for controlling them. This has led to debates between those who think they’ll be able to fix these problems, and others who believe companies should stop training new models altogether due to the risks.

If we continue trying to make models much smarter, such that they’re actually smarter than us … they will in fact be able to trick us successfully. And once you get to that point, many of the schemes that we’ve had at work up until now sort of go out the window.

The report goes out to point out that some researchers feel that executives at major AI companies have become “out of touch” with the severity of safety risks, though Axios was told that OpenAI is adopting newly introduced safety practices while Anthropic mentioned that “Keeping a model internal doesn’t make it safe,” adding that “we may slow down or hold back even when it costs us.”.

Ozempic is changing the way Americans shop and eat, even if they’ve never taken it

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1148 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fastcompany

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that the new class of drugs led by Ozempic and Wegovy don’t just have transformative effects on the people who take them – they’re reshaping the lives around them too.
  • The new class of drugs led by Ozempic and Wegovy don’t just have transformative effects on the people who take them – they’re reshaping the lives around them too.
  • In a recent development, patients prescribed GLP-1s are eating less and drinking less, but those behavioral shifts are trickling down to people in their life who aren’t taking the medications themselves.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that the new class of drugs led by Ozempic and Wegovy don’t just have transformative effects on the people who take them – they’re reshaping the lives around them too. Patients prescribed GLP-1s are eating less and drinking less, but those behavioral shifts are trickling down to people in their life who aren’t taking the medications themselves. Nearly one in four U.S. consumers have adjusted the way that they shop, eat, and drink based on knowing other people who take GLP-1s, according to a new survey from market research firm Escalent. The survey homed in on a group that the market research group calls “echo consumers,” which refers to people who don’t take a GLP-1 themselves but are changing their habits based on others in their social circles who do. The survey included data from 315 U.S. and 335 U.K. respondents who haven’t taken a GLP-1 drug but know someone who does and report changes to their own behavior based on those social connections. “Much of the attention surrounding GLP-1 medications has focused on the people taking them, and those living in their households,” Escalent Europe Managing Director Melissa Bane wrote. “… For retailers, food and beverage brands and restaurants, that’s a significant consumer group whose changing habits have gone largely unnoticed.” Among the echo consumers, 42% reported exercising more, 36% said they consume more wellness products, and 27% are drinking less. When eating out, 49% said they are ordering less at restaurants when eating with someone taking a GLP-1, while 21% are opting for alternative activities instead of socializing while eating and drinking. Almost one in five say they have picked different gifts for GLP-1 users they’ve shopped for, and many say they are buying different food and drinks to bring along to social gatherings in light of smaller appetites and friends and family who aren’t drinking as much. Industry-shifting numbers While the new survey only offers a small snapshot of consumer behavior, GLP-1 medications are clearly causing some seismic cultural shifts that we’re only beginning to understand. In the U.S., a massive 11% of the population are at the moment prescribed GLP-1s and 15% say they have tried them for weight loss before. That huge swath of Americans is already walking, running, and cycling more, buying fewer sweet treats, spending less on groceries, and drinking less alcohol. Habit shifts among GLP-1 users alone already represent a massive amount of change for industries to adapt to across just a few short years. Beyond those consumers, Escalent’s survey suggests that there are 1.7 times as many people shifting their behavior in light of the widespread use of weight management drugs than there are GLP-1 users. If similar numbers play out in future research, that’s an even more massive chunk of the population suddenly eating, drinking, and buying differently than they did prior to the advent of drugs like Ozempic, Wegovy, and Zepbound. “For Echo Consumers, a box of chocolates or a bottle of wine may no longer be the gift of choice, and social occasions could increasingly revolve around activities rather than going out for food and drink,” Bane said, calling the changes a “major shift” that will be even more evident during the holiday season. “Brands, retailers and hospitality businesses will need to find ways to adapt their offerings to reflect changing demand as these habits continue to spread through social networks.”.

Recent findings suggest that A short clip can help a project in different ways. It can show an idea you have not filmed, put an existing design in motion, or give an announcement something to look at. The same approach will not work if the clip needs to demonstrate a real feature or show exactly what happened. Before choosing a generator, decide what the viewer needs to learn from the shot.

Recent findings suggest that this article uses Kling 4.0 as a worked example, but the decision process applies to any AI video generator. It covers how these tools turn prompts and images into video, how Kling 4.0 and a few alternatives differ, how to choose a starting mode, how to add exact text and branding outside the generated clip with a short ffmpeg script, and when real footage is the better choice. Feature details come from each vendor’s own pages at the time of writing and change often, so confirm current terms before you strategy a production.

Sources indicate that ● Generated video is best for imagined shots. It suits concepts, backgrounds and early explorations, not instructions or faithful records.

Recent findings suggest that ● Your starting material decides the mode. A written idea, a reference image or a pair of opening and closing frames each call for a different input.

● Keep exact wording out of the generated clip. Titles, dates and logos belong on separate layers in an editor.

Recent findings suggest that ● Tools differ on control, cost and licensing. Compare inputs, length, resolution, credits and terms before you commit.

● Always review. Watch the whole clip at its final size and check it against the real product or design.

Sources indicate that most current systems extend diffusion models across time. A model learns to turn noise into a coherent set of frames guided by a prompt, and sometimes by an image or a clip. The research paper Video Diffusion Models describes this extension from images to video. The practical consequences are easy to observe.

● The prompt describes change over time. One visible change and one camera instruction usually work better than a long list of actions.

● Reference material steers but does not lock. A picture can suggest shape and colour without guaranteeing an exact match.

Recent findings suggest that ● Longer clips give more room for drift. Faces, logos and fine text are the first things to change between frames.

It has been revealed that ● Cost grows with length and resolution. Most hosted tools charge credits per second, so short previews are cheaper than full shots.

If you only have an idea, start with text. For a short announcement, you might ask for a band of light to move across a wall of coloured tiles. No one needs to recognise a particular wall, so the model can decide how it looks. Give it one visible change and a clear view of the subject. A prompt such as Soft morning light travels slowly across a wall of blue ceramic tiles. Fixed camera, no lettering is enough to see whether the idea works.

If you already have an illustration or a photo, reference mode gives you another starting point. Suppose you want a short concept clip for a desk accessory that only exists as a drawing. The picture can show the general shape and colour while the prompt describes the view you want. A video reference can help when it is the motion that is hard to explain, such as a slow camera slide. Say what each asset is meant to guide, and do not add a clip just because you have one.

It has been revealed that use keyframes when a particular view matters at a particular moment. Start with an opening image. If a short reveal also needs to end with the object facing forward, add an ending image to show that view. That is different from a reference image that mainly highlights what the object looks like. Neither method guarantees an exact match, so check the result rather than assuming the uploaded picture has locked the design.

No single tool fits every project. The table summarizes what each option’s own page states, and “not stated” means the page did not say, not that the feature is absent.

Reading the table: hosted studios such as the one on JXP are the quickest way to test an idea and need no setup, but you pay per second and work within their supported inputs. Kling’s own site is the place to check announcements and API options directly, since its page claims little about durations or resolution. Runway positions its models for motion quality and prompt following, while Google’s Gemini API video documentation suits teams building generation into their own products. The Diffusers video guide covers open-source pipelines for developers who want local control and are ready to manage GPUs and licences.

Trying an idea before making it. An illustrator might want to see how an imagined landscape feels when the light changes. A quick clip gives the team something to discuss: is the change visible, and does it happen at the right pace? It does not need to be the final animation to answer those questions.

Showing a product concept. A rotating view or a slow camera move can help people discuss how a design might be presented. It is useful early, when the shape and lighting are still being explored. Once the clip represents a product someone can buy, the standard changes. If a port moves or a button appears that the real product does not have, it is the wrong clip for that job.

In a recent development, making a short visual for a post. A few seconds of moving colour can give an event announcement or a project revision a distinctive opening. Put the name, date and other exact wording in your editor so they are readable and easy to change. The background only needs to support the message. If it competes with the text, use less movement or keep the background still.

According to recent reports, generated video is unreliable at lettering, so add titles in an editor or with a script. The command below overlays a title on a generated background and then checks the file properties. It assumes you already have a clip named background.mp4 and ffmpeg installed.

-vf "drawtext=text='Launch Night | 12 March':fontcolor=white:fontsize=64:x=(w-text_w)/2:y=(h-text_h)/2:box=1:boxcolor=black@0.35:boxborderw=24" \.

-c:v libx264 -pix_fmt yuv420p -an announcement.mp4.

ffprobe -v error -select_streams v:0 \.

-show_entries stream=width,height,r_frame_rate,duration \.

-of default=noprint_wrappers=1 announcement.mp4.

Sources indicate that because the text lives in the command, you can reuse the same background for three events by changing one string. The font may need to be set with a fontfile option on some systems. This is the practical version of keeping the moving background in one file and the editable details in another.

If people will follow the clip as instructions, use real footage or a screen recording for the steps. A convincing shot of an app is not proof that a button is in the right place. A generated close-up of a product is not a reliable way to show how its parts fit. You can still use an imagined opening, but make the switch to the real demonstration clear.

Think about revisions, too. If your team expects to adjust the same title, logo or date every week, put those elements on separate layers in an editor. And if the only movement you need is a slow zoom on an approved picture, apply that zoom directly. There is no reason to risk changing the picture when a simple edit will do.

It has been revealed that this matters when someone else will maintain the video. A reusable announcement template is easier to hand over if the moving background is one file and the event details are editable. If the team likes the movement but needs three versions with different dates, they can reuse the same clip. If every change calls for a newly introduced generation, the time you saved on the first version may disappear on the second.

The Kling 4.0 video generator on JXP currently offers 720p and 1080p settings and clip lengths from 3 to 30 seconds. According to its page, reference mode accepts up to 10 images and 5 videos, keyframe mode takes a first frame, middle frames and an optional last frame, and credits are charged per second with a higher rate at 1080p. For a first attempt, choose the frame shape you plan to use and make the clip only as long as it needs to be. Check the displayed credit cost before generating, because a short preview can tell you whether the direction works before you spend on a longer shot.

Decide what a good result looks like before you generate it. For the tile background, you need to see the light move without distracting from the words you will add. For a product concept, check whether the shape stays recognisable as the viewpoint changes. Watch the whole clip at the size the audience will see it. If the shot misses the point, revise one thing at a time: the motion, the framing or the source image.

It has been revealed that ● Read the licence. JXP’s page lists a commercial use license on each initiative and indicates outputs are for creative and lawful use, with the user responsible for reviewing them. Other tools have different terms.

Industry observers note that ● Do not misrepresent products or events. A generated clip should not suggest features or footage that do not exist.

Recent findings suggest that ● Consider provenance. C2PA is an open standard for Content Credentials that records where content came from and how it was edited, and some tools support it.

● Disclose where required. Follow platform and advertising rules on labelling AI-generated or altered content.

● Fine text, logos, hands and fast motion can drift or flicker between frames.

● Reference images and keyframes steer the result but do not guarantee an exact match.

● Vendor specifications, such as resolution and length, can differ between a model announcement and a particular platform.

● Long or exact sequences are often cheaper and safer to film than to generate.

Use text when you only have an idea, reference mode when you have a picture or clip to guide the look, and keyframes when specific views matter at specific moments.

Pick one such shot, try it, and put it next to the material you already have, and compare at least one alternative before you commit. If the project needs exact instructions or a faithful record, use the real thing. A useful first result is one that does its job in the edit, not simply one that looks impressive on its own.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Following its debut on the Galaxy Watch 9 earlier this year, Samsung is finally rolling out Wear OS 7 to older Galaxy Watch models with its One UI 9 Watch update.

Samsung’s One UI 9 Watch enhancement is largely focused on latest health features including Vitals, Heart Health Score, Daily Cardio Load, Fitness Index, and improvements to both Sleep Coaching and Sleep Apnea alerts.

“Vitals” is perhaps the most useful day-to-day addition, with Samsung Health collecting data on key vital signs such as heart rate, heart rate variability, respiratory rate, skin temperature, and blood oxygen and establishing a range so you can see when your vitals are out of the usual range.

One UI 9 Watch is based on Wear OS 7, and also includes an improved Compass app with “Track Back,” a feature that helps customers to follow their route back to a recorded point.

There’s also a new “Portrait Watch Face” that can adjust the clock face around the subject of a photo.

Industry observers note that samsung is, as of today, officially rolling out One UI 9 Watch with Wear OS 7 to the Galaxy Watch 8 and Galaxy Watch 8 Classic. Meanwhile, the update is in beta for several other older models which will be updated soon including:.

The Galaxy Watch 5 series and Watch FE should also be getting the upgrade, but no beta is available for those devices. Samsung’s first Wear OS watches, the Galaxy Watch 4 series, will not get the update.

Ukraine downs Russian jet-drone with cheap high-powered laser for the first time

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (497 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Tomshardware

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Ukraine has shot down a Russian jet-powered Shahed drone using an air defense laser, reports the Kyiv Independent.
  • For the first time, Ukrainian forces have shot down a Russian jet-powered attack drone using a laser weapons system.
  • Flash explains that the Blysk is at the moment being tested in active duty to protect an unnamed "critical infrastructure facility" [machine translation of Telegram post content].
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ukraine has shot down a Russian jet-powered Shahed drone using an air defense laser, reports the Kyiv Independent. This is a first for the 'Blysk' laser system, developed by Ukraine's defense tech manufacturer Carmine Sky, and which was deployed on November 19. The news was supported by a Telegram post with embedded video shared by Serhii 'Flash' Beskrestnov, the defense tech advisor to President Zelensky.

For the first time, Ukrainian forces have shot down a Russian jet-powered attack drone using a laser weapons system. https://t.co/PV9xTu3pdkNovember 25, 2026.

Flash explains that the Blysk is at the moment being tested in active duty to protect an unnamed "critical infrastructure facility" [machine translation of Telegram post content]. Though only in testing for a few days, it seems to have already been a success, as it is the first time a laser has been used to destroy one of the speedy latest jet-powered drones Russia has begun to deploy in the conflict.

It has been revealed that the 'Geran' drones mentioned by the source publication are Russian adaptations of the Iranian Shahed drones. Russia has used multiple iterations of the Iranian design, dubbed the Geran-2, Geran-5, etc.

Despite the celebratory post highlighting the first jet drone laser kill, Flash was realistic about the technology's potentially slow rollout. "It is still too early to discuss serial production of the laser," wrote the tech advisor on Telegram.

It isn't only Carmine Sky that is working on laser defense tech, noted Flash. This highly complex and capital-intensive battlefield tech is being worked upon by "several companies in Ukraine," it was claimed. We've also seen lasers touted as attractive anti-drone solutions by other nations.

Even if they might be expensive to develop, lasers are often praised for their low cost per shot. Blysk reportedly has a power output of 4kW, and using a shot of energy of this magnitude is far cheaper than firing a missile, for example. We've seen it claimed that the UK's DragonFire laser weapon costs roughly £10 ($13) per shot in energy consumption, and the Blysk cost per shot is probably in the same ballpark.

The source report states that weather hasn't been ideal for laser defenses recently, with "persistent cloud cover and fog." Unlike missiles and bullets, common weather phenomena like cloud cover can seriously weaken a laser beam before it reaches its target. Lasers will likely therefore never replace kinetic forms of air defense, but will be deployed to augment existing protections.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Major League Baseball sued its players’ association in federal court on Wednesday, asking that its contemplated lockout next week be declared legal and trying to head off any attempt by the union to decertify and challenge the work stoppage with an antitrust case.
  • Major League Baseball sued its players’ association in federal court on Wednesday, asking that its contemplated lockout next week be declared legal and trying to head off any attempt by the union to decertify and challenge the work stoppage with an antitrust case.
  • Industry observers note that in a 38-page complaint filed in U.S.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Major League Baseball sued its players’ association in federal court on Wednesday, asking that its contemplated lockout next week be declared legal and trying to head off any attempt by the union to decertify and challenge the work stoppage with an antitrust case. In a 38-page complaint filed in U.S. District Court in Manhattan, MLB and the corporate entities owning its 30 teams sued the Major League Baseball Players Association and the eight players on the union’s executive subcommittee, including record-setting pitcher Tarik Skubal. “MLB brings this action to keep the dispute over the next collective bargaining agreement (‘CBA’) at the bargaining table, where federal law says it belongs,” the lawsuit says. “MLB has a reasonable and imminent fear that the Union will attempt to use the threat of antitrust liability to derail the collective bargaining process altogether in favor of antitrust litigation.” Baseball’s five-year labor contract expires at 11:59 p.m. Dec. 1 and owners are expected to immediately impose a lockout, which would be the sport’s 10th work stoppage since 1972. Owners have proposed a salary cap for the first time since 1994, when players fought off the proposal with a 7 1/2-month strike that led to the first cancellation of the World Series in 90 years. Owners asked for a declaratory judgment determining a lockout doesn’t violate antitrust laws and doesn’t amount to an unreasonable restraint of trade. They asked for a ruling that the federal courts lack jurisdiction to enjoin a lockout and for an order that the players be defined as a legal class, which if granted could block individual lawsuits. “The lawsuit filed today by MLB is completely frivolous,” the union said in a statement. “We will respond appropriately, but MLB’s decision to run to court in the middle of negotiations rather than bargain in good faith is incredibly disappointing.” Among the lawyers representing MLB are former Solicitor General Paul D. Clement and Keker, Van Nest & Peters, which worked on behalf of the union in litigation against government seizure of drug tests. “Today’s filing is a defensive measure simply intended to keep the parties at the bargaining table to work towards a new collective bargaining agreement and a full 2027 season,” MLB spokesman Glen Caplin said in a statement. “We believe the union is preparing to follow the playbook its new leadership has used against other major professional sports leagues by pretending to ‘disclaim’ its status as the players’ bargaining process.” Caplin referred decertification as a “nuclear option,” mirroring union head Bruce Meyer’s description of the salary cap proposal as a “nuclear bomb.” —Ronald Blum, AP baseball writer.

Owners have proposed a salary cap for the first time since 1994, when players fought off the proposal with a 7 1/2-month strike that led to the first cancellation of the World Series in 90 years.

Owners asked for a declaratory judgment determining a lockout doesn’t violate antitrust laws and doesn’t amount to an unreasonable restraint of trade. Among the lawyers representing MLB are former Solicitor General Paul D. Clement and Keker, Van Nest & Peters, which worked on behalf of the union in litigation against government seizure of drug tests.

“Today’s filing is a defensive measure simply intended to keep the parties at the bargaining table to work towards a new collective bargaining agreement and a full 2027 season,” MLB spokesman Glen Caplin stated in a statement. “We believe the union is preparing to follow the playbook its new leadership has used against other major professional sports leagues by pretending to ‘disclaim’ its status as the players’ bargaining process.”.

#138617. The most dangerous election disinformation campaigns

📅 25 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 10m • 📚 Deep Dive (1970 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Fastcompany ↗ Open Full Page

The most dangerous election disinformation campaigns

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (1970 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fastcompany

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • You scrolled through your feed, and a video clip of a candidate’s speech popped up.
  • It has been revealed that you scrolled through your feed, and a video clip of a candidate’s speech popped up.
  • Industry observers note that candidates and their supporters spent a whopping $80 million to make AI-generated ads, as part of what AdImpact projected will be the most expensive election cycle on record.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

You scrolled through your feed, and a video clip of a candidate’s speech popped up. It doesn’t matter who you planned to vote for, the video struck an emotional—and negative—response. The clip was not AI-generated; the candidate really uttered the words you found upsetting. But the story the video told was fundamentally false. That was the 2026 midterms. Candidates and their supporters spent a whopping $80 million to make AI-generated ads, as part of what AdImpact projected will be the most expensive election cycle on record. This is one attempt to capture eyeballs and sway voters. Another is through foreign interference. In just one example, researchers tracking a Russian influence operation recently found a fake video masquerading as a Mother Jones report that captured over 11 million views. But disinformation is not stopping at deepfakes. Authentic videos that are repurposed and stripped of context represent a fresh frontier. I am not talking about a mere twisting of words. What we’re seeing is next level. THE NEW LOOK OF DISINFORMATION Think about the recent catastrophic flooding in Nepal and India. Some footage released within hours of the floods, intended to showcase the magnitude of the disaster, turned out to be from entirely different events. The footage was authentic. It just happened to be from a glacial flood in Alaska, a landslide in Japan, or a flood that occurred years before. These videos racked up millions of views. They also caused panic among friends and relatives trying to find information about their missing loved ones, and they potentially hindered rescue efforts by confusing the locations where help was needed. Now, consider the same tactic applied in the political sphere—real speeches and words taken drastically out of context, coming from events that could have happened years earlier. One of the most notable examples involved Michigan’s recently elected Democratic Senator Abdul El-Sayed. In August, he was eviscerated by Republicans for apparently calling for Sharia law to take over in America. Social media went crazy. Was the clip real? Yes, it was from a speech he gave in 2022. But the meaning was quite different when you look at its entirety in context. So different that Politifact gave it a “pants on fire” rating for its meaning being distorted. In Georgia’s hotly contested Senate race, Democratic Senator Jon Ossoff ran an ad of Republican Mike Collins urging Americans to get off Social Security and return to work. But that’s not exactly how it went down. The audio came from a broader conversation about tax policy, government revenue, and workforce participation. Collins was not saying retirees should get back into the workforce and lose their benefits (Politifact rated this one as “mostly false”). In both cases, the recordings were authentic. The misleading impressions came from stripping away the information necessary to understand what was being stated, not from manipulating the original material. You may believe that this is just par for the course in a political campaign, but just because something is common does not make it safe, normal, or acceptable. THE IMPORTANCE OF CONTEXTUAL UNDERSTANDING This tactic is becoming effective for two main reasons. Video is now our most prominent data source. Everything is recorded, so if someone is looking for a soundbite to make someone look bad, there is plenty of material available, if they’re willing to dig for it. The second issue is more technical. Deepfake detectors look for signs of manipulation. Authentic videos pass that test. Determining whether a clip is deliberately misleading requires a new set of inquiries, identifying when and where the video took place, what was happening around it, and what the broader context revealed. Making such determinations traditionally has taken a lot of people a lot of time to dig through archives. Even with the deep war chests candidates possess, they’re not going to devote the human resources needed to debunk every false video, at least not in time for that work to make a dent in the video’s impact. So, campaigns take hits, and candidates can spend considerable time and energy trying to explain past comments and rebuild trust. WHAT’S THE FIX? In 2026, voters and media companies are learning that two things can simultaneously be true: A clip can be legitimate while what it depicts is inaccurate. Voters are overwhelmed with election messages. Expecting them to research every clip they see is highly unlikely. Candidates and their backers count on this. Media companies and social platforms bear a greater responsibility, however. Fact-checking and moderation capabilities are essential to reduce the rapid spread of disinformation. Interestingly, while generative AI can be used to create convincing fakes, a different application of AI can be a powerful tool for identifying misleading content and stopping its spread. As good as AI is getting at generating realistic videos, it’s also getting good at understanding them. Solutions that can read a video and its contextual clues can be indispensable in determining whether an authentic video is being misrepresented online. Imagine an instant army of agent fact-checkers. When AI understands video the way a human does, it recognizes not only what is said and who’s speaking, but what else is on the screen and what the setting looks like. It can also search massive archives to see if that moment has appeared anywhere else. And, at the agent layer, tech can flag suspicious content, assembling supporting evidence and escalating cases to human reviewers in minutes. The technology that helps media companies and platforms find original footage, restore full context, and flag misleading claims will enable a faster response, not just to political ads but any sort of controversial content that might catch fire. Stopping the spread of disinformation is a perpetual problem. Thankfully, we are now building intelligent tools that can help. Jae Lee is CEO and cofounder of TwelveLabs.

According to a new report, Motorola’s next Razr flip phone is getting some major upgrades and a massive schedule change, with Motorola Razr (2027) launching early next year.

Android Headlines today published a upcoming set of images of the Motorola Razr (2027), as well as key specs. The device is shown in three colors and apparently carries the codename “Raptor.”.

There are several key spec changes here, including:.

In a recent development, motorola Razr (2027) is still only set for three Android OS updates and this new model is heavier at 195g (likely due to the bigger battery), but Motorola is very clearly making some substantial upgrades here. The biggest change is to the displays, both of which now match the Razr+ and Razr Ultra models. Some key specs, such as 8GB of RAM and 256GB of storage, are unchanged from the 2026 release.

Motorola has been releasing its Razr series in the Spring, but today’s report claims that Razr (2027) will launch in January 2027, likely at CES and at the same time as the Razr Flex book-style foldable. There’s no word on new Plus or Ultra models yet.

#138614. Workers hoard AI knowledge to stay competitive, Anthropic report claims

Workers hoard AI knowledge to stay competitive, Anthropic report claims

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (505 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fastcompany

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, AI tools are becoming increasingly ubiquitous, but the best techniques for using them are likely still a secret.
  • AI tools are becoming increasingly ubiquitous, but the best techniques for using them are likely still a secret.
  • This is because workers who develop highly effective AI tricks have no incentive to share them with their colleagues or their bosses, notes a report published Monday by Anthropic.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, AI tools are becoming increasingly ubiquitous, but the best techniques for using them are likely still a secret. This is because workers who develop highly effective AI tricks have no incentive to share them with their colleagues or their bosses, notes a report published Monday by Anthropic. Researchers interviewed 66 executives, managers, and employees at 58 of Anthropic’s corporate customers and found that many workers are reluctant to share their best AI tricks, citing reasons ranging from job security to more leisure time. The practice has frustrated managers looking to exploit AI-driven efficiencies. The report quotes one exasperated executive saying, “They don’t want you to know, because they want to use those 10 hours a week to go walk their dog.” AI hoarding is a fresh form of the age-old workplace phenomenon of knowledge hiding, in which employees deliberately withhold information from their coworkers to retain a competitive edge. Employees in the AI age have even more at stake: their jobs. If the trick they develop is powerful enough, they might render themselves redundant. And even for those whose jobs are secure, revealing a time-saving trick might just mean they are assigned more work. That raises a thorny question for business leaders: How do you incentivize employees to help automate their own jobs? Employers hoping to discourage AI hoarding may need to rethink how they measure and reward productivity. Otherwise, employees might realize that their most valuable professional asset is something they’re better off keeping secret.

That raises a thorny question for business leaders: How do you incentivize employees to help automate their own jobs?

Employers hoping to discourage AI hoarding may need to rethink how they measure and reward productivity. Otherwise, employees might realize that their most valuable professional asset is something they’re better off keeping secret.

AI companions are the most demanding consumer use of large language models right now. A coding assistant can forget your last message and still be useful. A companion that forgets your name, your running story, or the initiative you made last Tuesday has failed at its one job. On top of that, users now expect voice calls that feel like a phone conversation, not a walkie-talkie exchange with a five-second pause.

Sources indicate that three engineering problems decide whether a companion app works: how much of the conversation fits in the model's context window, what the app remembers once the window fills up, and how fast the voice pipeline answers. Here is how consumer companions handle each one, with real tier and pricing examples, and what developers can take from their designs for their own products.

Most LLM products are judged on single answers. Companions are judged on continuity. That creates pressure in three places at once:.

Every consumer companion is a different set of trade-offs across those three constraints, and the trade-offs are increasingly how the apps are priced.

Recent findings suggest that the context window is the total number of tokens the model can see when it writes the next reply. In a companion app, that budget is spent before the user states anything:.

When the chat log outgrows what is left, the oldest messages fall out. The user experiences this as the companion "forgetting" mid-conversation. This is why context size is now a headline spec in the category, and a paid feature. SpicyChat AI, for example, gives free accounts a 4K context window, then scales memory to 8K on its $19.95/mo tier and 32K on its $29.95/mo tier. Janitor AI runs about 9K of context on its own JanitorLLM. Independent uncensored AI chat benchmarks record these context sizes alongside refusal behavior and pricing, because context length predicts how long a roleplay stays coherent better than any marketing claim.

Some apps sell memory in messages rather than tokens. Fantasy GF's pricing page lists a 60-message base "smart memory" and 5x that, 300 messages, on its Ultra blueprint. Others sell it as a memory multiplier on higher subscription tiers. The pattern is consistent across the category: memory depth is the upgrade lever, not the model itself.

According to recent reports, no consumer app keeps an entire relationship in the prompt. Persistent memory is a separate system that writes to storage and reads back into the context window on each turn. In practice it has three layers:.

The differences customers notice are usually retention policies, not algorithms. Crushon AI's own subscription docs say free-initiative chat history is deleted after 7 days of inactivity, while paid plans keep it for the membership period. Paid tiers across the category commonly promise that memories never expire. There is also a security angle worth stating plainly: companion chat logs are among the most sensitive data a consumer product can hold. A 2024 breach at Muah.ai, first reported by 404 Media, exposed roughly 1.9 million users' email addresses together with their private prompts. Any app that builds persistent memory is also building a liability, and developers copying the pattern should treat the memory store as the most protected part of the system.

A voice call in a companion app is three models chained together: speech-to-text, the LLM, and text-to-speech. Run them strictly in sequence and a single reply can take several seconds, which reads as dead air. The apps that feel fast attack each stage the same way:.

With every stage streaming, time-to-first-audio can land close to a second on a good connection, which is roughly the threshold where a conversation stops feeling laggy. Voice is also expensive to run - three model calls instead of one, plus audio bandwidth - which is why it is metered harder than text. Fantasy GF charges 8 tokens per minute for voice calls (4 on Ultra), which turns the 100 monthly tokens on its entry blueprint into about 12 minutes of call time. SpicyChat, for its part, only adds text-to-speech at its top tier. Latency engineering and unit economics are the same problem here: faster pipelines cost less per call, and cheaper calls are what make voice viable below the top plan.

Tier details below come from each app's own pricing or documentation pages, checked November 16, 2026, and cross-checked against il.ly's AI companion testing guide, which hands-tests 15 companion apps across memory, media, and voice.

Two takeaways from the table. First, nobody sells a bigger base model - they sell a bigger window into the same one. Second, the free tiers are deliberately memory-poor: limited context and short retention are the upgrade prompt.

Even if you never build a companion, these apps are a useful reference architecture for any stateful LLM product:.

Recent findings suggest that consumer AI companions have turned three hard infrastructure problems - bounded context, durable memory, and real-time voice - into their pricing pages. Context size, memory depth, and voice access are the tiers. If you are building anything stateful on an LLM, this category is worth watching closely: it is solving continuity and latency problems at consumer scale, in public, one subscription tier at a time.

Industry observers note that it is the total amount of text, measured in tokens, that the model can consider when writing its next reply. The character definition, stored memories, recent chat, and the newly introduced message all share that budget. When the conversation exceeds it, the oldest content drops out and the companion appears to forget.

Sources indicate that yes, through a memory system separate from the context window. Apps summarize older chats, extract stable facts about you into a profile, and retrieve relevant past moments into the prompt. Retention varies: some free tiers delete chat history after as little as 7 days of inactivity, while paid intends typically keep memory for the membership period.

A voice turn runs three models - speech-to-text, the LLM, and text-to-speech - instead of one, plus audio transfer. Providers pass that cost on through per-minute token charges or by locking voice behind higher tiers.

For casual chat, 4K to 9K tokens works. For long-running roleplay or a companion expected to hold plot threads for weeks, 32K and up, or a well-built memory layer on top of a smaller window, makes the visible difference.

#138609. Innovation doesn’t scale on its own
